brand.title: Fabric cockpit shell
brand.summary: Navigation, command launch, and runtime telemetry stay fused into one operator cockpit above every authored workbench lane.

command_spotlight.title: Global operator quick-actions
command_spotlight.summary: These are the shell-level commands that should stay one gesture away no matter which workbench is active.

workspace_switcher.title: Global lane navigation
workspace_switcher.summary: Each lane chip mirrors an authored workbench page so the shell keeps one workspace model instead of inventing separate host tabs.

system_rack.title: Fabric runtime telemetry
system_rack.summary: Core registry scale and known seams stay visible in shell chrome so the workbench pages can stay focused on authoring surfaces.
notes: shell telemetry should read like instrumentation, not like a second inspector rail
registry counts and bridge seams belong in persistent chrome because they shape operator trust across every lane

operator_notes.title: Shell system guidance
operator_notes.summary: The cockpit should feel like one durable editor frame. Workbench pages should read like mounted subsystems, not isolated demo cards.
notes: command spotlight remains shell-owned so operators can bootstrap, switch lanes, preview, and publish without hunting through page-local inspectors
workspace chips mirror authored page descriptors and should be the future landing zone for semantic top-tab rendering in the native host
runtime status, registry counts, and extension seam warnings belong in shell chrome so lane pages can stay focused on authored work

workspace_pages.hero_title: Scene-first assembly and ingest mission control
workspace_pages.hero_summary: Stage layout, intake, placement, and downstream review stay in one operator surface instead of scattering across separate host-owned tools.

workspace_pages.title: Sculpt And Modeling Forge
workspace_pages.hero_summary: Brush operations, topology refresh, and publish invalidation are grouped as one sculpt workbench instead of separate one-off inspectors.

workspace_pages.title: Rig And Animation Bench
workspace_pages.hero_title: Graph, timeline, and deformation review in one bench
workspace_pages.hero_summary: Rig sync, clip blocking, and viewport validation share one workbench so animation state stays coupled to the same authored contracts.

workspace_pages.hero_title: Plan, cache, and review simulation work as a first-class lane
workspace_pages.hero_summary: This page keeps simulation planning visible, links it to downstream render and comp work, and makes the current solver seam honest instead of pretending it is complete.

workspace_pages.title: Render And Composite Control Room
workspace_pages.hero_title: Review renders, composite plans, and final publish risk in one control room
workspace_pages.hero_summary: Render and comp should feel like a real production room with visible outputs, not a final step hidden behind a single preview button.

workspace_pages.hero_summary: The delivery lane should own bundle readiness, recurring jobs, and release artifacts without forcing operators to leave the authored session model.
